newsitem.title: USA: Morgan Stanley says card losses moderating.
newsitem.headline: Morgan Stanley says card losses moderating.

text.p: Morgan Stanley Dean Witter Discover & Co is seeing a "slowing in the rate of increase" of writeoffs in its credit card unit, the company's chief strategic and administrative officer said Wednesday.
"There are also signs that the rate of increase in chargeoffs is beginning to moderate," the executive, Thomas Schneider, told analysts during a conference call.

In the company's fiscal second quarter ended May 31, credit card and transaction services rose three percent from the year earlier, reflecting a 49 percent increase in the provision for loan losses on a managed loan basis, Schneider noted.

He said bankruptcies were running ahead of the company's plan while writeoffs other than those related to bankruptcies were slightly below plan. The percentage of writeoffs related to bankruptcies was not significantly different from the long-term trend.
Schneider said Morgan Stanley had not reached the point of saying writeoffs would go down, but it was changing its tone to reflect a more optimistic view of the card business.
Morgan Stanley Dean Witter Discover & Co was formed May 31 by the merger of Morgan Stanley Group Inc and Dean Witter Discover 7 Co.

The net charge-off rate in the managed portfolio was 7.07 percent in the three months ended May 31, compared with 5.22 percent a year earlier and 6.91 percent in the three months ended February 28, 1997. The delinquency rate was 6.90 percent compared with 5.79 percent year-over-year and 7.49 percent in the quarter ended in February.

Robert Scott, chief financial officer, said the company had a strong quarter in securities despite some slowing in March and April. He said there were currently no plans or authorization to repurchase shares, but the company was studying the issue of its capital needs.
